newsitem.title: USA: Human Genome achieves milestone in deal with Roche.
newsitem.headline: Human Genome achieves milestone in deal with Roche.

text.p: Human Genome Sciences Inc said Tuesday that it has achieved its first and only milestone in its agreement with Swiss drugmaker Roche Holding Ltd to sequence the Streptococcus pneumoniae genome, a bacterial pathogen.
The company did not disclose any financial terms.

It said that under a March 1996 agreement, Roche gave it an upfront payment, a milestone related to sequencing, and royalties on certain products in exchange for the right to develop new drugs based on Human Genome's genetic data.

In a separate agreement, Human Genome also said it will provide Roche with a non-exclusive license to use the sequence information from Enterococcus faecalis, a major component of hospital-based infections, to identify anti-infectives and antibiotics in return for an upfront payment and royalties on certain products.
In May of this year, Human Genome announced that it had determined the genomic sequence of this bacteria.
The company did not disclose financial information about the agreement.
